extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism closeout using the existing worker-5 placeholder as prior evidence only; mechanism claims are re-grounded in primary text and figure locators.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Freshly dissolved HBA(111-142) disrupts L. monocytogenes bacterial membranes, causing intracellular content leakage.
direct_assay_types: transmission electron microscopy of treated bacteria

supports: body text states FD-HBA disrupts bacterial membrane and causes leakage
TEM and liposome dye leakage panels

mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct evidence is strongest for L. monocytogenes and bacterial-lipid liposomes under the reported assay conditions; do not generalize to all bacteria or eukaryotic membranes.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Agitated HBA(111-142) binds/aggregates bacteria and promotes macrophage uptake rather than directly killing L. monocytogenes in the survival assay.
mechanism_claims.mechanism_category: bacterial aggregation and phagocytic clearance support

supports: body text reports E. coli aggregation and increased macrophage uptake

mechanism_claims.limitations: Macrophage uptake support is in vitro and should be framed as promoted uptake/clearance, not direct in vivo efficacy.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Agitated HBA(111-142) inhibits enveloped herpes/measles virus infection by acting early during infection and binding virions, but it is not virucidal in the TCID50 experiment.
mechanism_claims.mechanism_category: viral attachment/entry interference without virucidal inactivation

supports: body text reports early-step inhibition, virion binding, and no virucidal titer reduction
time-of-addition, TEM virion binding, and TCID50 panels

mechanism_claims.limitations: Antiviral activity is selective: local source reports no effect on SARS-CoV-2, IAV, or ZIKV and no anti-HSV-2 activity for FD-HBA.
